issues.description: The UML/problem statement defines Pneumatic.openValve() as a no-argument method, and the solution's implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower, LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement openValve() with no parameters. However, the solution's Pneumatic interface declares openValve(int duration) with an int parameter. This creates a method parameter mismatch between the interface and its implementations and contradicts the UML. As written in the solution repository, this will cause compilation errors (implementing classes do not match the interface) and will confuse students about the correct signature they must implement based on the UML/problem statement.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the Pneumatic interface with the UML and the implementing classes. Change the interface declaration to: void openValve(); (no parameters). Alternatively, if the intent was to have a duration parameter, update the UML/problem statement and the implementing classes to use openValve(int duration). The recommended fix is to remove the parameter from the interface so it matches the UML and the implementations, preventing compilation errors and student confusion.
